title: Exposure Canvas: Latency-aware Fractional Allocator for Canary & A/B Releases
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement an extensible policy engine (Exposure Canvas) that computes per-cohort fractional traffic allocations for canary and A/B model introductions using latency-aware heuristics, confidence bounds, and safety decay schedules. The engine should support staged steps, ramp/decay curves, shadow probing lanes, and automatic rollback triggers based on configurable telemetry contracts.
objectives: Provide deterministic, reproducible fractional allocations for release steps
Make allocation decisions that respect SLO targets (p99 latency, error rate) and cost constraints
Enable fast, safe rollback when regressions are detected
Expose observability hooks and explainability for allocations
acceptance_criteria: API to accept release policy and produce step-by-step allocations (percentages) for cohorts
Support latency-weighted allocation that reduces exposure to variants with degraded p99 by 50% within one step
Rollback action automatically queued when regression thresholds breached for 3 consecutive minutes
Integration tests covering staged rollout with shadow probes and simulated backend latency regressions
Console shows per-step expected vs. actual traffic and rationale (top contributing metrics)
tasks: Draft policy DSL for Exposure Canvas (syntax, fields, defaults)
Implement allocator core: input validation, scheduler, decay curves
Integrate telemetry inputs (p50/p95/p99, error rate, request volume) from Console API
Add shadow-probe orchestration: create shadow lane, sample % routing, collect differential metrics
Build rollback manager: hysteresis window, cooldown timers, automated fallback to previous model
Create e2e harness to simulate cohorts and verify guardrail behavior
Add UI surface in Console for visualizing allocations and manual overrides
Write unit + integration tests; performance bench for allocator at 100k TPS
risks: Telemetry latency may cause oscillations in allocation; mitigate with smoothing windows and commit hysteresis
Complex policies increase cognitive load—provide sane defaults and a policy linter
Interactions with Dedicated autoscaling may change latency distribution; coordinate with infra team during rollout
notes: We will reuse rollout telemetry contract defined by runtime-telemetry RFC (link) and extend with a 'stability_score' metric
Consider conservative default: max step increase 10% and max cohort exposure 30% until 1 hour of stable telemetry
Prefer declarative policy with optional 'explain' flag to surface decision path for audits
